title: Desk Note: Live-Listing Limits and the Primary-Residence Rule for Listings
content:
# Desk Note — Live-Listing Limits and the Primary-Residence Rule

Applies to Roamhaven Listings whenever a listing would go live: when it is published, relisted, brought back from a snooze, or reinstated.

## The rule

Before a listing goes live, the host's portfolio is checked.

1. **Host account status.** A listing can go live only when the host account's status is active. The status is read from the host account the listing belongs to, as Roamhaven's system records it at the time of the change; the host's own description of the account does not establish it.
2. **Tier limit.** The number of the host's live listings — the host's listings on the same host account whose status is listed or snoozed — is counted as it stands before the change. That number must be below the most live listings the host account's tier allows under the Host Accounts charter. Otherwise the listing stays in its current status until another listing of the host leaves live status or the host's tier rises.
3. **Primary-residence rule.** In a jurisdiction whose jurisdiction entry has the primary-residence rule (among Roamhaven's six jurisdictions, Denver, CO-DENVER), a host may hold only **1** live entire-place listing. The count covers the host's entire-place listings on the same host account, in the same jurisdiction, whose status is listed or snoozed, as they stand at the time of the change. Listings of hosted space types are not counted.
4. **Snoozing frees no slot.** A snoozed listing is still live, so snoozing a listing does not free a slot under either count.

## The conditions side by side

| Condition | Read from | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| Host account status | the host account the listing belongs to | the status is active |
| Tier limit | the host's listings on that host account that are listed or snoozed, before the change | the count is below the tier's live-listing figure |
| Primary-residence rule (jurisdictions with the rule only) | the host's live entire-place listings in that jurisdiction | holding the listing live keeps the host at no more than 1 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical portfolios)

- A host whose tier allows 3 live listings holds 2 listed listings and 1 snoozed listing. The count is 3, which is not below 3, so a fourth listing does not go live; it stays in its current status.
- The same host unlists one of the listed listings. The count falls to 2, which is below 3.
- A host with an active account holds one listed Entire Apartment in Denver. A second Entire Home in Denver would make 2 live entire-place listings there, above the figure of 1.
- A host account whose status is restricted cannot have a listing go live, whatever the counts show.
